Vital signs: not dictated today.

Testing Results

Creatinine 2.4 this morning, up from 1.9 yesterday. Potassium 5.2. Urine output 600 mL overnight. Renal ultrasound pending.

Assessment

Patient is a 69-year-old with acute kidney injury presenting with rising creatinine and reduced urine output. Creatinine has increased from 1.9 to 2.4 over the past 24 hours, with overnight urine output of 600 mL. Potassium is elevated at 5.2. Physical examination reveals dry mucous membranes and no edema. Bladder scan shows 90 mL post-void residual. The clinical picture is consistent with acute kidney injury, possibly related to volume depletion given the dry mucous membranes and reduced urine output. Renal ultrasound is pending to evaluate for structural causes. The patient is currently receiving intravenous fluid support at 75 mL per hour. Management will focus on optimizing renal perfusion, monitoring electrolytes, and determining whether dialysis will be needed if renal function continues to decline.

Plan

1. Continue intravenous fluids at 75 mL per hour; recheck basic metabolic panel this afternoon to reassess creatinine and electrolytes.
2. Obtain renal ultrasound as pending to evaluate for structural abnormalities or obstruction.
3. Avoid nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and contrast agents.
4. Monitor urine output closely; consider dialysis if creatinine continues to rise.
5. Continue home tamsulosin.
